title: When Did They Rise and Fall? A Comparative Timeline of the Ancient Civilizations
repository: TDOE Grade 6 World History & Geography standards (cluster date ranges)
citation: Tennessee Department of Education, Grade 6 World History and Geography academic standards (public domain).
alt_text: Horizontal timeline with one bar per civilization (Mesopotamia, Egypt, Israel, India, China, Greece, Rome) spanning its BCE/CE date range, so students can compare which overlapped and which came first.
data_source: TDOE Grade 6 standards cluster date ranges (Mesopotamia c. 3500-1700 BCE; Egypt c. 3000-700 BCE; Israel c. 2000-500 BCE; India c. 2500-400 BCE; China c. 2500 BCE-200 CE; Greece c. 800-300 BCE; Rome c. 500 BCE-500 CE)

title: Why They Needed the Rivers: Climate of the Fertile Crescent (Baghdad)
repository: NOAA NCEI (GHCN / World Meteorological Organization climate normals)
citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, WMO/GHCN climate normals for Baghdad (public domain).
alt_text: Climograph of Baghdad: bars of very low monthly rainfall (near zero in summer) with a temperature line peaking above 40C, showing an arid environment that required river irrigation to farm.
data_source: NOAA NCEI monthly climate normals for Baghdad, Iraq (mean monthly precipitation and temperature)

title: The Gift of the Nile: The River's Annual Flood Cycle
citation: W. Willcocks, Egyptian Irrigation (London/New York: Spon, 1899), Nile discharge tables (public domain, pre-1929). Corroborated by O. Toussoun, Memoire sur l'histoire du Nil (1925).
alt_text: Line chart of mean monthly Nile River flow across the year, low in spring and surging to a peak in August-September, illustrating the predictable annual flood that deposited silt and set the farming calendar.
data_source: Willcocks, 'Egyptian Irrigation' (mean monthly Nile discharge / gauge readings tables)

title: How Tall Were the Pyramids of Giza? Comparing the Three Great Pyramids
repository: Internet Archive / UCL Petrie Museum (public-domain text)
citation: W. M. Flinders Petrie, The Pyramids and Temples of Gizeh (London: Field & Tuer, 1883), survey measurements (public domain).
alt_text: Bar chart comparing the original heights of the three main Giza pyramids (Khufu ~146 m, Khafre ~143 m, Menkaure ~65 m), with a small human/modern-building reference bar for scale.
data_source: Petrie, 'The Pyramids and Temples of Gizeh' (measured original heights and base lengths of Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure)

title: Life on the Monsoon: Mumbai's Rainfall Concentrated in Four Months
citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, WMO/GHCN climate normals for Mumbai (public domain).
alt_text: Bar chart of mean monthly rainfall for Mumbai showing almost all precipitation falling June-September, illustrating the summer monsoon that shaped agriculture in ancient India.
data_source: NOAA NCEI monthly climate normals for Mumbai, India (mean monthly precipitation)

title: The Yellow River's World: Climate of the North China Plain (Zhengzhou)
citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, WMO/GHCN climate normals for Zhengzhou (public domain).
alt_text: Climograph for a Yellow River city showing warm-summer, cold-winter conditions with rain concentrated in summer, the seasonal pattern that shaped early Chinese farming on the loess plain.
data_source: NOAA NCEI monthly climate normals for Zhengzhou, China (Yellow River valley; mean monthly precipitation and temperature)
